extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and registered patent agents filing applications at IPOS (Singapore)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing and filing a patent application (Patents Form 1 and related forms) at the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore, including timelines, document formats, priority claims, formalities checks and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate for exhibition (officially recognised exhibitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to file a certificate issued by the authority responsible for the exhibition stating (a) the invention was exhibited there; (b) the opening date of the exhibition, or if first disclosure did not take place on the opening date, the date of the first disclosure; (c) an identification of the invention, duly authenticated by the authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate must be filed within 4 months from the date of filing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period applicability (post-30 Oct 2017 applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent applications filed on or after 30 Oct 2017, the grace period provisions listed in Chapters 6.1.18 to 6.1.24 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the specified chapters for details; the document flags that different rules apply depending on filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Number on Patents Form 1
rubrics_metrics.description: While a reference number is optional, applicants are encouraged to provide one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reference number assists identification of the patent application and correspondence, especially useful for applicants with multiple applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments on filing (Specification tab)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must attach the abstract, description, claims, sequence listing (if any) and drawings (if any) in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim(s) are not required to be furnished at the time of filing to obtain a date of filing; claims must be submitted to the Registry within the time period specified in Chapter 2.2.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted document formats for specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may file patent specifications in DOCX (Microsoft Word) or PDF; DOCX is the preferred format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer DOCX for ease of processing; both formats are accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic document size limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of each document uploaded in electronic form cannot exceed 100 MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents exceeding 100 MB must be split into parts not exceeding 100 MB each. If there are more than three (3) parts, email ipos_enquiry@ipos.gov.sg for information on how attachments may be split and filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming date of filing of earlier Singapore application
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to claim the date of filing of an earlier Singapore application as the date of filing of this application under Sections 20(3), 26 or 47(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claiming of an earlier date of filing must be made at the point of filing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to indicate divisional or Registrar-ordered filings
rubrics_metrics.description: For a divisional application filed under Section 26, choose the option 'Filing for a divisional of an earlier Singapore application'. For an application filed in response to an order by the Registrar under Sections 20(3) or 47(4), choose 'Filing in response to an order by the Registrar regarding the entitlement of earlier Singapore application'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting the correct option ensures the system treats the application appropriately and auto-populates parent details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent application details and priority editing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the parent application number is entered, parent details (title, declared priority date(s), inventor names) auto-populate. The earlier application number and its date of filing must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional may, but need not, claim priority declared on the parent. It is possible to edit auto-populated information (e.g., remove a priority claim). A divisional cannot make a claim of priority which was not claimed in the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The title is a formal requirement and must be provided. It must be short, precise and indicate the matter to which the invention relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar may reframe the title if it fails to comply; as the title is published, applicants may wish to avoid disclosing excessive detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of priority(s) under Section 17(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration must be made if the applicant is claiming priority on one or more earlier relevant applications; for each earlier application, its filing date and country must be furnished at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier application's application number is available, it should preferably be provided; otherwise provide before the end of 16 months from the declared priority date. A copy/translation is not required at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of priority via Form 57 (late filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may apply to restore a declaration of priority even though the subsequent application was not filed within 12 months from the earliest relevant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must be done by filing Patents Form 57 within 14 months from the date of the earliest relevant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a late priority claim via Form 57
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may apply to add a claim of priority where they had failed to make a declaration of priority in an application filed within 12 months from the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File Patents Form 57 within 16 months from the date of filing of the earlier relevant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of declared priority date via Form 57
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to correct a mistake in the declared priority date may be done on Patents Form 57 within 16 months from the declared priority date if it causes the declared priority date to be changed to a different date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Chapter 11.2 for more details on addition, correction or late declaration of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of declared priority date
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to remove the declared priority date may be submitted in writing via eCommunications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar will consider the request; one consideration is that removal should not revive an abandoned application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply and ownership of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (individual or corporate) may apply for a patent alone or jointly. The right to the patent belongs primarily to the inventor(s) but can belong to any person entitled by rule of law or enforceable agreement (e.g., employer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is not the inventor, identify the inventor(s) and state how rights were derived (e.g., assignment, employment contract).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide UEN/entity code for Singapore corporates
rubrics_metrics.description: Singapore companies or applicants who have prior filings are encouraged to provide their UEN or entity code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing UEN/entity code facilitates management of IP with the Registry, auto-retrieval of applicant information and centralised updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant name and address requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant is an individual, the full name, address, nationality and country of residency must be furnished. Where the applicant is a corporate, provide corporate name, country/state of incorporation and address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sole proprietors or partnerships must provide details of the sole proprietor or all partners; names must be indicated in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor identification and derivation of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor is the actual person who devised the invention and cannot be a body corporate. An applicant who is not the inventor must identify inventor(s) and state how rights were derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more inventors are not applicants, details of inventors must be indicated on Patents Form 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Inventorship and Right to Grant (Patents Form 8) timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more inventors is not an applicant, a Statement of Inventorship and of Right to the Grant of a Patent (Patents Form 8) must be filed within 16 months from the declared priority date, or in the case of a divisional, on the day of filing Patents Form 1, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Form 8 is not submitted within the timeline, the application may be treated as abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation of rights entry requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must indicate how the rights have been derived from the inventor(s) (e.g., contract of employment, assignment) under Derivation of Rights (Patents Form 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct basis is selected and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-organism deposit under Budapest Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the option if the specification refers to micro-organisms deposited with an International Depository Authority under the Budapest Treaty; provide the depositary name, deposit date and accession number in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If details not available at filing, provide within 16 months from declared priority date or filing date; other earlier deadlines apply if the Registrar publishes earlier or receives a request for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of earlier application (where no description filed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description is not filed but is incorporated by reference to an earlier relevant application, the following must be provided within the timeline: (a) a written notice confirming incorporation and that the description is completely contained in the earlier application as filed; (b) the description; (c) a copy of the earlier application and its English translation, if any; (d) Patents Form 56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy/translation need not be filed if previously filed at the Registry. This section appears only when no specification has been uploaded in the Specification tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address for service in Singapore
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of any proceedings, an address for service in Singapore must be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For corporate applicants, indicate a staff name under representative or C/O to ensure prompt attention to correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent representation details
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent is appointed, the agent should select the box for agent and indicate his UEN, name and address for service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing telephone number and email is recommended to facilitate immediate clarification; all official correspondences will be sent via IPOS Digital Hub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent ceasing to act (Form CM1) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agent intends to cease to act, he must provide in Form CM1: (a) a notice of such intention; (b) the party's latest address (including email) on the agent's records; (c) a statement that the agent has given reasonable notice to the party and informed the representee of consequences if no substitute agent or address provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new Singapore address for service is not furnished in Form CM1, the Registrar will issue a notice; consequences apply if no address for service provided within two months after the Registrar's notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for the grant of a patent must be signed in this part of the form by the applicant, each applicant (if more than one), or by the authorised agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where filed electronically, the application may be signed with a text string signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee timing and payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For securing a date of filing, the filing fee is not required on the day of filing; the applicant has 1 month from filing to decide whether to proceed and must pay the filing fee within 1 month from submission of the document indicating a patent is sought or Patents Form 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment methods: Internet Banking, Visa/Master credit and debit cards, and GIRO. The filing fee timeline is not extendable; failure to pay within timeline results in abandonment. Deferred payment is available for electronic submission; use 'Deferred Payment' under 'Payment' menu in IPOS Digital Hub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation and format of application number and entity code
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of Patents Form 1 an application number is allocated. With effect from 14 Feb 2014 the format is TTYYYYXXXXXC where TT = type of application (10 = national application), YYYY = year, XXXXX = running numbers, C = check alphabet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant named is a Singapore corporate, the UEN must be entered; other entities will get an allocated entity code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing formalities checks (initial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a date of filing is allocated, the Formalities officer will check: (a) there is an indication that a patent is sought or Patents Form 1 is filed; (b) the applicant(s) are clearly identified; (c) a description of invention or a letter indicating incorporation by reference is submitted; (d) for divisionals, additional checks on parent number validity, filing timing, that divisional is filed before parent is refused/withdrawn/abandoned, and that the divisional is filed by original applicant or successor in title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements not complied with, the Formalities officer will issue a letter and the applicant has 2 months from date of the letter to make observations and/or file missing documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and forms for missing/incorrect formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: If requirements missing, applicant may submit missing documents via eCommunications, amend Patents Form 1 via Patents Form 13, correct obvious errors via Form CM4 (indicate relevant rule), or add/correct priority claims via Patents Form 57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant needs more time to respond, an extension of time may be requested; otherwise the application shall be treated as abandoned. The registry will make an entry in the Patents Journal of refusal/abandonment where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing determination rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of filing will be the earliest date when all documents satisfy the requirements in Chapter 2.5.1. If any required documents are submitted later, the date of filing may be shifted to the later date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate that if description is filed after Form 1, the date of filing becomes the description lodgement date; for divisionals, they retain the date of filing of the earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling attachments indicating >100MB
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant selects the box indicating attachments exceed 100 MB, the request will be put on hold until documents are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of filing will be the date that the documents are received at the Registry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-organism deposit information provision deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If 'Micro-Organism Deposited under the Budapest Treaty' was selected, provide name of depositary, deposit date and accession number in the specification either at filing or: (i) within 16 months from declared priority date or filing date; (ii) before the date of a request for early publication; (iii) before 1 month after notification that a request for inspection has been received, whichever is earliest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely provision avoids adverse formalities actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fee non-extendable timeline and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing fee must be paid within 1 month from submission of Patents Form 1 or document indicating a patent is sought. The time period for payment is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not paid within the timeline the application will be abandoned and an entry made in the register and Patents Journal. If payment made after the timeline, the applicant will be informed and a refund initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority application number furnishing timeline and removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a declared priority date, the applicant has up to 16 months from the earliest priority date to furnish the application or file number of each priority application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not furnished within timeline, the Formalities officer will notify and the priority claim will be removed. Applicant may request multiple extension(s) up to 6 months via Patents Form 45 before the end of 6 months from expiry; further extension possible only if the applicant satisfies Registrar of continuing intention to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent claims filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims must be filed within 12 months from the declared priority date, or 2 months from the date of filing, whichever is later. If no priority date, claims must be filed within 12 months from date of filing. For divisional applications, period is 2 months from lodgement of the divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period for filing claims is not extendable. Claims may be submitted via eCommunications with document type 'Claim(s) Only'. If not submitted within the timeline the application will be abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any document or part of a document filed at the Registry is not in English, an English translation should be submitted together with the document. If notified by the Registrar to submit a translation, the English translation and the Verification of English translation (VET) should be submitted within 2 months from the date of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translations not provided within timeline, the Formalities officer will proceed to refuse the application. Applicant may request multiple extensions of time up to 18 months from the original timeline via Patents Form 45; further extension possible only upon satisfying the Registrar of continuing intention to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — Patents Form 56 deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has up to 3 months from the date of filing of the application or from the initiation date for a divisional application to submit Patents Form 56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Patents Form 56 is not filed within the timeline, the application will be abandoned and an entry made in the register and Patents Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination checklist (formalities examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: During preliminary examination the Formalities officer will check numerous requirements including: (a) Patents Form 1 is filed; (b) Singapore address for service furnished; (c) address of each applicant furnished; (d) declaration of priority is within 12 months; (e) where date of filing accorded based on a description filed, no incorporation by reference to a priority application is made; (f) names and addresses complete; (g) title on Form 1 corresponds with title in specification; (h) number of sheets indicated matches actual number filed; (i) an abstract is filed; (j) the abstract indicates 1 or 2 figures for publication; (k) no drawing or part of description missing; (l) specification commences with an appropriate title; (m) the description, claims and abstract do not contain drawings; (n) drawings are executed in black, sufficiently dense and dark strokes; (o) documents are legible and suitable for direct reproduction; (p) documents commence on a new sheet, sheets are numbered consecutively, with drawings numbered as a separate series; (q) where inventor details are provided, the relevant section in Patents Form 1 should be indicated as 'No' if not all applicants listed are inventors and derivation of right should be filled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any requirements are not met, a Formalities Examination Adverse Report will be issued; applicant may amend using Patents Form 13 within 2 months from the date of the letter. Replacement sheets must be submitted for amended documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of permissible amendments via Patents Form 13
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that may be made using Patents Form 13 include: (a) amendment(s) of abstract, description, claims, or drawings; (b) amendment(s) on option(s) selected on Part(s) of Patents Form 1; (c) amendment(s) on the number of sheets indicated on Patents Form 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing Form 13 in response to a Formalities Examination Adverse Report, enter the IPOS Reference Number from the report and select 'In response to the Registrar’s Formalities Examination Adverse Report'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to respond to Formalities Examination Adverse Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request multiple extensions of time up to 18 months from the original timeline to respond to a Formalities Examination Adverse Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for extension should be made on Patents Form 45 before the end of 18 months from expiry of the original timeline. Further extension beyond 18 months is possible only if applicant satisfies the Registrar of continuing underlying intention to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Refusal and status update
rubrics_metrics.description: If other formal requirements are not met by the timeline, the Formalities officer will issue a Notice of Refusal of Application. The application status will be updated as 'Refused (EOT possible)' on the register and an entry will be made in the next Patents Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application does not meet priority and missing part checks, the applicant will be informed that the priority or missing part will be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of Formalities Examination report and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: When all formal requirements have been met, a Formalities Examination report will be issued to the applicant and an entry will be made in the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may then request a search report (Patents Form 10), search and examination report (Patents Form 11), examination report (Patents Form 12) or supplementary examination report (Patents Form 12A) if not already requested. If the Formalities Examination report is issued after timelines for search/examination procedures, the applicant may request an extension for the Registrar to consider extending the timeline to file those requests on a case-by-case basis (e.g., delay in issuance by the Registry).
